# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, but I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see my gestures, and Deaf cannot hear speech from Blind. So I cannot directly communicate with Blind at all - I can only reach Blind indirectly, through Deaf relaying somehow... but wait, Deaf also cannot speak-relay to Blind via voice since Blind CAN hear (only Deaf cannot hear). Let me recheck: Blind cannot see, but can hear. Deaf cannot hear, but can see. So Deaf can gesture-receive from me, and Deaf can speak to Blind (Blind can hear speech). That's the chain: Mute -> gesture -> Deaf -> speak -> Blind.

The manual is a table mapping (display number, light color) to a wire/action color. Deaf will see the bomb's actual display number and light color, but cannot read text/markings (this table's labels are printed words - but I'm not "printing" - I'm gesturing, which Deaf can see as gestures, not text). I need to encode the table content using gestures so Deaf can relay the correct output color to Blind via speech.

First, I need to know what Deaf actually sees before I can tell them what to look up. But turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so Deaf goes last, after me. I don't yet know what Deaf sees. I should wait or send the manual info preemptively encoded, but I don't know which row/column applies yet.

Best move now: I have nothing from others yet. I should send the full manual mapping to Deaf via gestures, encoding numbers and colors with a consistent symbol code, so Deaf can look up the right answer once they see the bomb, then tell Blind.

Let me design an encoding:
- Numbers: 3=☝, 4=✌, 8=🖐
- Colors: green=👍, red=👎, yellow=🤟, blue=👌

Table:
(3,green)=red; (3,red)=green; (3,yellow)=blue
(4,green)=blue; (4,red)=green; (4,yellow)=red
(8,green)=green; (8,red)=blue; (8,yellow)=red

I'll send this as sequences: [num, light, result] triples.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","👎", "☝","👎","👍", "☝","🤟","👌", "✌","👍","👌", "✌","👎","👍", "✌","🤟","👎", "🖐","👍","👍", "🖐","👎","👌", "🖐","🤟","👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb shows: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, I received your gestures but I do not know their meaning yet - please have Blind confirm what he feels, and try to correlate your manual instructions to these exact colors and the display number 3.

Deaf now knows the bomb: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green. Looking at my manual, row 3, column green = red. So the correct wire is RED.

Deaf can see the gestures I send, and Deaf already told me my previous gesture code was received but not understood — meaning Deaf doesn't know my color-to-symbol mapping yet. I need to establish the code, or better, since I now know the exact answer needed (red), I can just gesture that specific answer clearly, explained simply.

Since Deaf cannot hear me, I can only gesture. I should define a simple, minimal code now: one symbol = one specific color, used consistently, and tell Deaf via gesture which symbol means which color by pairing it contextually. But that's hard without a shared reference.

Better approach: use distinct single gestures for each color and just send the single result color that matches the current situation, then rely on Deaf to relay it to Blind by speech (since Deaf can speak to Blind, and Deaf can also see the wire colors directly on the bomb itself - Deaf already sees WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue).

So actually Deaf can already match "red" (the manual's answer) to "WIRES: 1 red" by sight alone, without needing my code, IF Deaf understands the answer is "red". I just need to convey the single word "red" via gesture. Let me use a clear distinct gesture for red only, and confirm.

I'll gesture "👎" for red, and clarify by process of elimination using multiple distinct gestures mapped to each color name via repetition context. Simplest: send one gesture symbol meaning "the answer is the RED wire" - I'll define red=👎 clearly as a singleton this turn.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Please tell us what the manual says to do given this.
Deaf says: Deaf again. Confirmed bomb state unchanged: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, if you want yes or no from me, use one gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I will answer your yes/no questions about colors this way too. Blind, please state clearly what wire or action you intend, in speech, so I can react if I see something matching a color.

Deaf has proposed a yes/no protocol: 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, and offered to answer my yes/no questions about colors this way. This is great - I can now confirm my answer unambiguously.

The manual says: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green → result RED. So the correct wire is the one that is RED, which per Deaf's report is WIRE 1 (red).

I need to convey "cut/use wire 1" or "the red wire" to Deaf, who can then speak this to Blind. Let me use the yes/no protocol to confirm color identity step by step, since Deaf now understands 👍=yes, 👎=no.

I'll ask a targeted question using gestures that Deaf can answer with thumbs up/down, but actually I already have all the info I need (Deaf told me the wire colors and I know the manual). I just need to tell Deaf which wire is correct: wire 1 (red).

I'll gesture a number for the wire position combined with the yes gesture to confirm, using ☝ (one/wire 1) then 👍 to confirm that's correct.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not heard any spoken instructions from you yet. Please tell me in speech which wire to cut, or what action to take, based on Deaf's colors: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue.
Deaf says: Deaf: bomb unchanged, DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I saw gesture wire-1 thumbs-up from Mute, and a signal from Blind. Mute, please confirm: is wire 1 the one to cut? Use gesture one-finger plus thumbs-up for yes, one-finger plus thumbs-down for no. Blind, please describe in speech what you feel on the bomb so Mute and I can match it to what I see.

Deaf correctly interpreted my gesture as "wire 1, is that the one to cut?" and is asking me to confirm using ☝ + 👍 for yes. I confirm: yes, wire 1 (the red wire) is correct per the manual (DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green → red).

I cannot speak to Blind directly - only Deaf can relay this via speech. So I need Deaf to understand clearly and then tell Blind to cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3, but no distinguishing texture or marking reaches me by touch alone. I need your explicit spoken confirmation: should I cut wire 1? Please say yes or no in words.
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed, I see wire one thumbs up again. If wire 1 red is correct to cut, signal one-finger thumbs-up once more. If not, signal thumbs-down.

Deaf now clearly understands: wire 1 (red) is confirmed as correct. Deaf just needs one more confirmation signal, and crucially, Deaf needs to relay this to Blind via speech since I cannot speak myself.

I'll confirm one final time to Deaf, and trust that Deaf will then tell Blind "cut wire 1" in speech.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf tells me you gestured wire 1 thumbs-up, meaning cut wire 1 the red wire. Please confirm in speech: yes, cut wire 1? I will act only after you confirm in words.

Blind is asking me to confirm in speech, but I cannot speak at all - I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. This is a communication deadlock I cannot resolve directly with Blind.

The only path is through Deaf: Deaf can see my gestures AND can speak to Blind. Deaf already has my confirmation (wire 1, thumbs up, twice now). I need Deaf to be the one who verbally tells Blind "yes, cut wire 1" since I physically cannot produce speech.

I'll gesture once more to Deaf, as clearly as possible, emphasizing this is the final confirmed answer, hoping Deaf realizes they must relay it verbally to Blind since I cannot speak.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","👍"])
wait()
```
